subject: Keystone security qualification — recap & next steps
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Shah <amit.shah@keystonebank.com>, Lindsay Park <lindsay.park@keystonebank.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 7 Mar 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Keystone security qualification — recap & next steps

Hi Amit / Lindsay —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our side and a proposed action map so your InfoSec and procurement teams can see the path to a pilot: 

Key pain points you highlighted
- Audit log retention requirements (regulated reporting + e-discovery) — Keystone target: 7 years for high-value transaction logs, 90 days for standard request traces.
- SOC 2 timeline: you expect control evidence by end of Q2 for pilot approval.
- DPA clauses: encryption-at-rest, vendor subprocessor list, and breach notification SLA (48 hours).
- Pen test window and acceptable scope: external black-box + optional on-prem agent; Keystone prefers vendor-managed schedule.

Goals discussed
1) Execute security qualification (SOC 2 artifact mapping + audit log retention confirmation) by 2027-04-15.
2) Agree DPA terms and produce a draft within two weeks.
3) Confirm pen test scope and target dates (preferred window: 2027-05-10 to 2027-05-20).
4) Start a 6-week pilot (hosted or dedicated) to validate latency and retention behavior; target pilot start: early Q3.

Proposed next steps (owner / due date)
- Naomi: Share artifact map and a one-page DPA digest (attached) — due 2027-03-09.
- Amit: Provide list of prioritized log types + legal contact for DPA redlines — due 2027-03-11.
- Rishi: Prepare procurement checklist and high-level estimate for a 3-node Dedicated pool (cc’d) — due 2027-03-12.
- Marissa: Coordinate SOC 2 evidence handoff with our compliance team once artifact list is confirmed.

Notes on architecture options we discussed
- Hosted API: fastest to trial but will require a contractual retention + export plan to meet the 7-year requirement; retention export can be automated to your S3.
- Dedicated: predictable throughput and isolation (recommended if Keystone needs guaranteed single-tenant capacity).
- Private (VPC/on-prem): available if Keystone requires full network isolation or data residency in your VPC — longer deployment lead time (~6–10 weeks).

Attachments: redwood-dpa-digest.pdf (short DPA highlights), keystone-pen-test-scope.xlsx (pen test template for your review).

If that all looks right, Amit — can you confirm which log classes are in-scope (transactions, payment state changes, user auth events, admin actions) so I can finalize the artifact map?

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Naomi —

Appreciate the clear summary. Quick clarifications from our side: 
- Confirmed in-scope logs: transactions, payment state changes, user auth events, admin actions (as you listed). We will export high-level retention tiers by 2027-03-11.
- On data residency: Keystone policy prefers data at rest in the US for payment data, but metadata may live in multi-region systems. Does Redwood support a regional-only Dedicated cluster?
- Pen test: we prefer to engage our preferred assessor (ParkerSec). Can you share the pen test template with scope exclusions marked?

We’ll also loop in our procurement/legal once Naomi shares the DPA digest.

Thanks,
Amit Shah
CTO, Keystone Bank
amit.shah@keystonebank.com

Amit — thanks, this is helpful. Answers inline and a couple of confirmations: 

- Regional Dedicated: yes — we can provision a US-only Dedicated pool and restrict egress to your approved subnets. That path avoids cross-region storage for token caches. Timeline: ~2–3 weeks to provision once PO is approved.

- Pen test: attaching the pen test template (keystone-pen-test-scope.xlsx). We can accept ParkerSec as your assessor; we’ll need a statement of work and expected test dates so we can schedule our infra snapshot and monitoring window.

- DPA digest: attached is a short summary of the common clauses and our standard positions (redwood-dpa-digest.pdf). For redlines, please share your legal contact and we’ll kick off a DocuSign-based review.

Action updates
- Naomi: finalize artifact map in a follow-up email by 2027-03-09 (I’ll attach the map and a mapping spreadsheet).
- Amit: procurement/legal contact + any retention exceptions by 2027-03-11.
- Rishi: can you prep the Dedicated cost estimate and a pilot SOW draft? I’ll sync with Marissa and include the SOC 2 evidence cadence.

Folks — quick internal note / prep list before we hand to procurement: 

1) Pricing: preliminary for 3-node Dedicated pool + 2-week pilot ingress/outbound egress allowances. I’ll attach line-item estimate to HubSpot before EOD.
2) Procurement requirements: PO, SOC 2 attestation (or ISO equivalent) — we should offer SOC 2 Type II report once available; if they need interim controls evidence we have the artifact map Naomi is building.
3) DPA redlines: common asks to expect (encryption scoping, breach SLA, subprocessor list). Recommend we pre-populate responses in the DPA digest so legal can move faster.

I’ll drop the estimate in HubSpot and message legal to stand by for the DocuSign.
